projects.name: FITMAN
projects.one_line: Full-stack AI fitness and nutrition coach.
projects.problem: Personalized workout and nutrition coaching is hard to keep consistent without structured user context.
projects.goal: Workout generation, nutrition and progress tracking, and an AI coach with persistent memory and profile context.
projects.nabil_contribution: Built workout generation, nutrition and progress tracking, and an AI coach with persistent memory and profile context. The API uses token authentication, Pydantic validation and Row Level Security.
projects.architecture: React client → FastAPI → user context from Supabase → LangChain with Groq → safety checks → Supabase PostgreSQL.

projects.results: A public demo is live. User counts and production SLAs are not documented.
limitations: Not production: there are no documented users, SLAs or load tests.
LangGraph is a listed dependency, but the coach in the public repository calls LangChain with Groq directly.
projects.conflict_resolution: Source notes say planned and older site copy said Active Production. Status is active_development. Do not call FITMAN production. Use of LangGraph and rate limiting is stated on the resume, but the public code read on 2026-11-25 does not show either in use. Do not cite <300ms Groq latency as a verified benchmark.

projects.name: MediMatch AI
projects.one_line: Doctor matching and booking platform for Bangladesh.
projects.problem: Patients need to find a suitable verified doctor from symptoms described in their own words.
projects.goal: Take symptoms in English, Bangla or Banglish, show suitable doctors with live schedules, and book a time.
projects.nabil_contribution: Built a LangGraph assistant, vector search over doctors, transactional booking, and patient, doctor and admin web portals. Emergency rules run before any model, so an alert never depends on the LLM.
projects.architecture: React web app → FastAPI → emergency rules → LangGraph assistant → MongoDB vector search → Supabase Postgres. Postgres is the source of truth and MongoDB is only a search index.
projects.data_flow: Symptoms → emergency rules → LangGraph assistant → vector search → doctors re-read from Postgres → booking
decisions: Double booking is prevented with a Postgres exclusion constraint and row locking.
Only approved doctors can be found or booked.
Every table with user data has Row-Level Security.
projects.results: The repository records 1,120 passing backend tests and 130 Playwright tests, 20 simultaneous booking requests tested against one slot, and 48 attack attempts all blocked on the local stack. A 28-query retrieval evaluation on demo data reached 96.4% Hit@3 and 38.1% Precision@3. 7,537 directory doctors were imported, with 2,846 free-text specialties mapped to 28.
limitations: Not in production: the Flutter app and production deployment are still to come.
Retrieval was measured on demo data with 3 specialties, where a precision near 33% is close to random choice.
The assistant never diagnoses or prescribes, and its output guard is not a reliable filter on unseen replies.

projects.name: Nabil Portfolio Technical Digital Twin
projects.one_line: This repository's evidence-grounded RAG agent over structured portfolio knowledge.
projects.problem: Visitors need accurate answers about Nabil without marketing hype or hallucination.
projects.goal: Canonical knowledge → hybrid retrieval → claim-aware grounded generation.
projects.nabil_contribution: Designed and implemented the Next.js portfolio, FastAPI RAG service, MongoDB vector indexing, and digital-twin policy in this repository.
projects.architecture: Visitor → Next.js → FastAPI → query classification → entity resolution → canonical knowledge + MongoDB Atlas vector retrieval + lexical overlap → merge → LLM (OpenRouter) only when evidence exists → answer + confidence + sources + claims.
decisions: Canonical YAML knowledge is the source of truth.
Retrieval failure must refuse rather than use the model's latent biography.
Fast path answers come from structured knowledge, not a second hardcoded resume.
projects.challenges: Duplicate marketing copy vs source notes; inflated metrics in earlier UI.
projects.solutions: Claim taxonomy, provenance, honest FITMAN status, refusal when evidence is missing.
projects.results: Implemented in this repository. No published latency SLA.
projects.limitations: Dense retrieval depends on MongoDB being indexed with current knowledge. Lexical search works locally from YAML even if MongoDB is empty.
projects.future_improvements: Cross-encoder rerank, reproducible eval harness with live models.

projects.name: TEXTtoSQL
projects.one_line: Offline AI database assistant that runs from a USB drive on a 4 GB RAM PC.
projects.problem: Usual text-to-SQL tools need internet, an account or powerful hardware, and often return SQL that was never run.
projects.goal: Turn English into tested SQL with no internet, GPU or installation.
projects.nabil_contribution: Built the Windows app, the MariaDB sandbox, the retrieval, verification and repair loop, the benchmark, and a LoRA fine-tuning experiment.
projects.architecture: C#/.NET WinForms app → llama.cpp running Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B (4-bit) → private portable MariaDB.
projects.data_flow: Question → schema and similar examples → model writes SQL → run in sandbox → checks → repair → SQL and result
decisions: The rule was fixed in advance: replace the original model only if the benchmark improves.
projects.results: Scored 66/80 (82.5%) on a benchmark that compares query results, including 14/20 on the held-out database. The model was quantized from 3.1 GB to 986 MB. LoRA fine-tuning on 8,319 execution-checked examples lowered validation loss from 0.578 to 0.123, but the benchmark tied at 66/80, so the app ships the original model.
limitations: Experimental project with a small model: SQL that runs can still be wrong, and complex joins are its weakest area.
Failures on the first 60 benchmark questions guided development, so 14/20 on the held-out set is the fairest estimate.
